findings.finding: [Native, REPRODUCED/CODE] ON does not break a running program.

[Native, REPRODUCED/CODE] ON does not break a running program.

tests: native_side_input ON/next run; User nested-loop/INPUT cancellation tests

findings.finding: [Firmware, CODE] Live whole-calculator save/resume is absent.
findings.baseline:
[Firmware, CODE] Live whole-calculator save/resume is absent.
    Recovery stores durable OFF checkpoints and restarts the firmware; it does
    not serialize live CPU/thread/host state. Synthetic snapshot facilities are
    separate and do not provide a live calculator save-state button.
    Source: crates/prime-emulator/src/recovery.rs:1.

findings.finding: [Firmware, COVERAGE] The OS interface is far from fully implemented.
findings.baseline:

    Static registry: 742 service slots; 48 Implemented, 31 PartiallyImplemented,
    663 NotInvestigated/no handler. Full slot-by-slot inventory is attached as
    implementation-inventory.json. No-handler slots are coverage gaps; many
    are not used by common calculator flows. Do not turn 663 into a count of
    demonstrated broken features. The GUI uses ZeroReturn and reports observed
    unsupported call sites, so some unimplemented paths continue with 0.
    Source: crates/prime-emulator/src/services/{names,mod,handlers}.rs;
    crates/prime-emulator/src/session.rs:1373;
    crates/ppl-gui/src/ide/calculator.rs:88.

findings.expected_behavior: Used firmware OS services implement their real ABI; unhandled slots remain accurately inventoried.
implementation: Investigated separate from Native and repaired concrete thread/IRQ/debug services; inventory retained.
tests: service/ARM/synchronization/lifecycle tests
findings.verification: partial: 663 slots remain unhandled; exact signatures/resource ABI evidence and implementations required

findings.finding: [Firmware, CODE] Several registered OS services are still stubs/partial.
findings.baseline:
[Firmware, CODE] Several registered OS services are still stubs/partial.
    Suspend/Resume/WakeUp thread calls return 1 without the corresponding thread
    behavior. Interrupt enable/done return 1; registered ISR dispatch is not
    provided by this HLE route. SetAutoPowerOff returns 0. Debug printf logs
    the format string without formatting arguments. These are distinct from
    synthetic full-system hardware tests.
    Source: crates/prime-emulator/src/services/threading.rs:73;
    crates/prime-emulator/src/services/handlers.rs:75,643;
    crates/prime-emulator/src/services/system2.rs:120,162.
findings.root_cause: Deferred/thread control and IRQ masking were stubs; debug printf ignored varargs. Audit missed existing ISR dispatcher.
findings.expected_behavior: Thread suspension/resumption/termination, IRQ enable/done/dispatch and formatted debug output alter real execution state.
implementation: Deferred launch, suspension/resumption/termination, interrupt masking/reenable/done, deterministic ISR delivery/error propagation, bounded common ARM printf marshalling.
tests: thread_control6; svc16; sync_lifecycle6; emulator lib157; genuine local firmware lifecycle
findings.verification: partial: priority scheduling, wake semantics, auto-power-off and extended printf formats remain incomplete

findings.finding: [Firmware, CODE] Device/environment behavior is simulated in several paths.
findings.baseline:
[Firmware, CODE] Device/environment behavior is simulated in several paths.
    Battery status is fixed (full/not charging); USB/USBHOST/INDICATOR IOCTL
    paths simply succeed. Unknown devices return synthetic FF-filled output.
    Storage-capacity reporting fills only an observed field of the OS struct.
    These do not supply a faithful physical battery/link/device environment.
    Source: crates/prime-emulator/src/services/system2.rs:138,287-402.
findings.root_cause: Host device environment uses fixed/synthetic battery, USB and storage replies.
findings.expected_behavior: Firmware device replies reflect an implemented virtual battery/USB/storage/environment model.
implementation: Preserved existing simulated environment; no claim synthetic device replies are physical parity.
tests: service/device-state unit tests; code evidence in firmware report
findings.verification: unresolved: device contracts, changing virtual environment and observed OS struct layouts need implementation/ABI evidence

findings.finding: [Test tooling, CODE] calc_key is misleading for Native input tests.
findings.baseline:
[Test tooling, CODE] calc_key is misleading for Native input tests.
    The automation comment says it follows keypad behavior in either backend,
    but AutoStep::CalcKey invokes send_calc_transition, whose Native branch
    only updates held keys and never routes a press to Native Home. This audit
    used real click_calculator_key pointer events, separated by 80ms, for the
    final keypad evidence. Tests based on calc_key alone can miss UI behavior.
    Source: crates/ppl-gui/src/ide/automation.rs:114,666;
    crates/ppl-gui/src/app_firmware.rs:423-443.
findings.root_cause: Native calc_key automation bypassed the Native reducer.
findings.expected_behavior: Automation calc_key dispatches through the same production reducer as actual on-screen Native clicks.
implementation: calc_key invokes central production native dispatcher; held transitions remain distinct; waits include actual CAS/app/VM tasks. Added WaitDialog for real interaction synchronization.
tests: native_side_input21 behavior assertions; graph/state/dialog/User workflows
findings.verification: implemented
